stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing the range of actions the Board may take on a complaint. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An advisory letter is retained in the Board's files but does not constitute formal disciplinary action.
Dismissal of the complaint is not among the actions available to the Board.
A reprimand constitutes formal disciplinary action.
A censure is a severe reprimand.
Probation allows practice under conditions imposed by the Board.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.06 lists the available actions. Dismissal of the complaint is the first of them. An advisory letter is an official written document retained in the Board's files that does not constitute formal disciplinary action. A reprimand does constitute formal disciplinary action and a censure is a severe reprimand. Probation constitutes disciplinary action and consists of a period during which the registrant may practise under conditions imposed by the Board.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: retained in the files, yet expressly not formal discipline.
choice_analysis.B: Dismissal of the complaint is expressly one of the listed actions.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: a reprimand is formal disciplinary action.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: a censure is characterised as a severe reprimand.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: probation permits practice subject to Board conditions.

related_facts: Probation may be imposed pursuant to a formal adjudicatory hearing or a consent agreement.
explanation.mpje_trap: Only the advisory letter is written but non-disciplinary; reprimand, censure and probation are all formal.

reasoning_steps: Place each proposed action on the regulatory list
Separate the one non-disciplinary written action from the formal ones
Note that probation preserves practice under conditions
